nodes.name: Thrust-vector-control (TVC) actuators (merchant tier)
nodes.description: Electromechanical / electrohydraulic / electrohydrostatic actuators that gimbal launch-vehicle engine nozzles for steering. On SpaceX engines this function is captive: Merlin uses hydraulic pistons driven by the engine's own RP-1 turbopump pressure, and Super Heavy's gimbaling Raptors switched from hydraulic to an in-house electric actuation system after Starship flight 1. The genuine merchant TVC-actuator tier (Moog, Woodward) flies on OTHER programs (ULA Vulcan/Centaur, Antares, SLS-class upper stages), not on SpaceX engine cores.
nodes.notes: Captive-vs-merchant honesty: SpaceX engine TVC actuation is overwhelmingly in-house (Merlin fuel-pressure hydraulics; Super Heavy all-electric since 2023). Merchant actuator suppliers below are flight-proven on non-SpaceX reusable/expendable programs and represent the supply tier any reusable-launch program that does NOT vertically integrate would buy from. Single-source character: no public merchant supplies SpaceX's gimbal actuators; that corner is captive.

nodes.name: Propellant & pneumatic control valves (merchant tier)
nodes.description: Cryogenic-compatible propellant and pressurant control valves (ball, poppet, pilot-operated), engine control valves, and pneumatic/servo valves for launch-vehicle engines and stage fluid systems. Merchant suppliers (Moog, Woodward, Parker Aerospace, Eaton) sell these across the launch industry; SpaceX builds much of its own valve set in-house for Merlin/Raptor but the broader reusable-launch industry draws on this merchant tier.
nodes.notes: Merchant tier is real and multi-source for valves (Moog, Woodward, Parker, Eaton) — unlike actuators this is NOT a single-source corner. SpaceX-specific valve sourcing is not publicly disclosed and is substantially captive; the suppliers here are mapped at industry altitude (qualified across launch programs), not asserted as SpaceX's specific vendors.

nodes.name: Engine igniters / ignition systems
nodes.description: Spark-torch / augmented-spark igniters that light the main combustion chamber and preburner/gas-generator of liquid rocket engines. SpaceX uses in-house torch igniters on Merlin and a spark-ignition system on Raptor; no public merchant igniter supplier to SpaceX was found. This component is documented as genuinely captive at SpaceX with only a thin/absent public merchant tier for reusable-launch primes.
nodes.notes: GENUINELY CAPTIVE / no merchant source found: round-1 search surfaced only patent literature and prime-internal torch/spark igniter designs (SpaceX, NASA, Blue Origin), no merchant catalog igniter supplier to SpaceX. Honest miss recorded rather than a fabricated supplier. Woodward markets monopropellant/cold-gas valves and some ignition-adjacent controls for satellites but not a confirmed launch-engine igniter to SpaceX.

nodes.name: Precision bearings (engine turbopump / gimbal / cryogenic)
nodes.description: Precision rolling-element, spherical, and cryogenic self-lubricating bearings for engine turbopumps, gimbal/thrust-vector joints, and stage mechanisms in launch vehicles. Merchant bearing makers (RBC Bearings with flight-proven cryogenic FibriloidCR bearings for Space Launch Vehicle applications; Schaeffler; SKF) serve this tier; turbopump-internal bearings on SpaceX engines are not publicly sourced and are likely captive/custom.
nodes.notes: RBC's FibriloidCR is the cleanest named launch-vehicle bearing product (cryogenic, flight-proven for Space Launch Vehicle & satellite applications). Schaeffler/SKF are general precision-bearing majors reused from the parcel/bearing domain; their specific launch-engine turbopump bearing role is qualitative (industry-capability), not a confirmed SpaceX turbopump supply.

nodes.name: Metal additive-manufacturing machines (engine parts)
nodes.description: Laser powder-bed fusion (LPBF / DMLS) and large-format metal 3D-printing machines used to print rocket-engine hot-section and propulsion parts (injectors/injector heads, manifolds, combustion-chamber and turbopump components). SpaceX prints Raptor/Merlin parts on Velo3D Sapphire systems under a Sept-2024 licensing deal; EOS and Nikon SLM Solutions supply DMLS/LPBF machines used across the reusable-rocket-engine industry (ArianeGroup, Rocket Lab, LEAP 71).
nodes.notes: This is the one engine-adjacent component with a CONFIRMED SpaceX merchant supplier: Velo3D Sapphire printers in use at SpaceX for Raptor parts (2024-09-12 licensing deal). EOS (private) and Nikon SLM Solutions (Nikon subsidiary) are merchant LPBF machine suppliers to the broader reusable-rocket-engine industry; their direct SpaceX use is not publicly confirmed (reported_capable_supplier altitude).

nodes.name: Metal AM powder & specialty alloy feedstock (engine parts)
nodes.description: Aerospace-grade metal powders (nickel/cobalt/titanium superalloys; copper alloys for regen-cooled combustion-chamber liners) and specialty-alloy feedstock for additively manufactured and forged rocket-engine parts. Merchant suppliers include Carpenter Additive (Carpenter Technology) and ATI. SpaceX's GRCop-class copper liner alloy is NASA-developed and substantially captive/internally produced; the merchant powder tier supplies the wider engine-AM industry.
nodes.notes: Honesty on the hot-section: the GRCop-42/84 copper-alloy combustion-chamber liner used on Raptor/Merlin is a NASA-Glenn-developed alloy that SpaceX produces largely in-house — NOT a merchant purchase. Carpenter Additive (Ni/Co/Ti powders) and ATI (Ti + Ni superalloy powder for AM) are genuine merchant powder suppliers to the broader aerospace-engine AM market; treated as industry-capability suppliers, not confirmed SpaceX feedstock vendors.

nodes.name: Moog Inc.
nodes.description: U.S. precision-motion-control supplier; designs and manufactures launch-vehicle thrust-vector-control actuators (electromechanical, electrohydraulic, electrohydrostatic) and cryogenic propellant/pressurant control valves. Flight-proven TVC actuators on ULA Vulcan first stage, Antares first stage, Centaur and Ares upper stages — i.e. the merchant TVC tier for reusable/expendable launch programs other than SpaceX (whose engine actuation is captive).
nodes.notes: Ticker MOG.A (NYSE) verified 2026-06 via NYSE/Nasdaq listings (also MOG.B class B). Merchant relevance: TVC actuators + cryogenic engine control valves; flies on Vulcan/Antares/Centaur/Ares, not on SpaceX Merlin/Raptor (captive). listingStatus public.

nodes.name: Woodward, Inc.
nodes.description: U.S. control-systems supplier (Fort Collins, CO). Its Space & Defense business supplies launch-vehicle main-engine controls, thrust-vector-control actuation, flight-control actuation, control valves and servo valves, plus satellite monopropellant/cold-gas valves and gimbal actuation — a merchant actuation/valve tier for the launch industry.
nodes.notes: Ticker WWD (NASDAQ) verified 2026-06 via Woodward IR / exchange. Merchant relevance: TVC actuation + control/servo valves for launch vehicles; not a confirmed SpaceX engine-core supplier. listingStatus public.

nodes.name: Parker Hannifin Corporation (Parker Aerospace)
nodes.description: U.S. motion-and-control major; Parker Aerospace supplies engine fuel/lubrication/thermal-management systems, hydraulics, fluid-management, and aerospace valves for missiles, rockets and launch vehicles (e.g. NASA SLS and Orion; historical Space Shuttle and Apollo propellant-feed valves). Merchant fluid-systems/valve tier for launch.
nodes.notes: Ticker PH (NYSE) verified 2026-06 via Parker IR (investors.parker.com) / exchange. Merchant relevance: launch-vehicle fuel/fluid systems and valves (SLS/Orion named); SpaceX-specific role not disclosed. listingStatus public.

nodes.name: Velo3D, Inc.
nodes.description: U.S. metal additive-manufacturing OEM (Sapphire laser powder-bed-fusion systems for support-free complex metal parts). SpaceX uses Velo3D Sapphire printers to produce engine components including Raptor parts; in Sept 2024 SpaceX signed a non-exclusive licensing agreement (USD 5M technology licence + USD 3M engineering/support). The one engine-adjacent merchant supplier with a confirmed SpaceX relationship.

nodes.name: EOS GmbH (Electro Optical Systems)
nodes.description: German metal/polymer additive-manufacturing OEM; leading supplier of industrial DMLS (Direct Metal Laser Sintering, a laser powder-bed-fusion process) machines. EOS systems print rocket-engine parts across the launch industry — e.g. an ArianeGroup injector head consolidated from 247+ parts to one, and copper-alloy combustion chambers (with AMCM). Private (family/founder-owned), so no ticker.
nodes.notes: PRIVATE company (no exchange ticker — do not guess one). Merchant relevance: DMLS machines for rocket-engine injectors/combustion chambers; named users include ArianeGroup, Launcher, RUAG, Airbus D&S. SpaceX-specific use not publicly confirmed (industry-capability altitude). listingStatus private.

nodes.name: Nikon SLM Solutions AG
nodes.description: German metal additive-manufacturing OEM (Selective Laser Melting, LPBF), wholly-owned subsidiary of Nikon Corporation since Jan 2023. Supplies large-format metal 3D-printing machines (SLM-500, NXG-class) for reusable rocket engines — Rocket Lab MoU for ultra-large platforms; LEAP 71 full-flow staged-combustion (FFSC) injector heads in IN718; university reusable-engine programs with integrated cooling channels.
nodes.notes: Ownership: wholly-owned subsidiary of Nikon Corporation (Tokyo 7731.T); SLM Solutions delisted (Frankfurt) Sept 2023 after Nikon squeeze-out. Public exposure is via parent ticker 7731.T. Merchant relevance: LPBF machines for FFSC reusable rocket engines (Raptor-class cycle) — Rocket Lab/LEAP 71; SpaceX-specific use not confirmed. listingStatus subsidiary, ticker = parent.

nodes.name: Carpenter Additive (Carpenter Technology Corporation)
nodes.description: Business unit of Carpenter Technology Corporation supplying high-quality iron-, nickel-, cobalt- and titanium-based aerospace alloy metal powders for additive manufacturing. Powders feed AM rocket-engine and propulsion parts (copper alloys for combustion-chamber heat exchangers; Ni/Co superalloys for hot-section). Merchant powder tier for the engine-AM industry.
nodes.notes: Ticker CRS (NYSE) verified 2026-06 — Carpenter Additive is a business unit of Carpenter Technology Corporation (NYSE: CRS). Merchant relevance: aerospace AM metal powders (Ni/Co/Ti); GRCop copper-liner alloy on SpaceX engines is NASA-developed and largely captive, so Carpenter is mapped as industry-capability powder supplier, not a confirmed SpaceX feedstock vendor. listingStatus subsidiary (parent ticker).

nodes.name: ATI Inc. (Allegheny Technologies)
nodes.description: U.S. specialty-materials producer of titanium and titanium alloys, nickel- & cobalt-based superalloys, and metal powders (Ti, Ti-aluminides, Ni/Co superalloys) for additive manufacturing (DMLS / EBM). Supplies aerospace jet- and rocket-engine and airframe materials; merchant powder + mill-product tier for engine parts.
nodes.notes: Ticker ATI (NYSE) verified 2026-06. Merchant relevance: Ti + Ni/Co superalloy powders & mill products for aerospace engines and AM; industry-capability altitude (not a confirmed SpaceX-specific vendor). listingStatus public.

nodes.name: RBC Bearings Incorporated
nodes.description: U.S. precision-bearings manufacturer. Its Transport Dynamics FibriloidCR cryogenic self-lubricating spherical bearings/rod ends are tested and flight-proven for Space Launch Vehicle and satellite applications (-320 degF cryogenic to +450 degF); Western Precision Aero supplies gearbox/electro-mechanical gimbal assemblies for rocket thrust-vector functions. Merchant launch-vehicle bearing tier.
nodes.notes: Ticker RBC (NYSE) verified 2026-06 — RBC transferred its listing from Nasdaq to NYSE in Sept 2022, symbol unchanged 'RBC'. Merchant relevance: flight-proven cryogenic launch-vehicle bearings (FibriloidCR) + gimbal assemblies for thrust-vector. listingStatus public.

evidence.excerpt: In-house manufacturing of core building blocks - actuators, controllers, servodrives, and servomotors. ... Actuators can be combined with controllers for a thrust vector control (TVC) system solution.
evidence.limitations: Vendor (Moog) marketing page; good for what Moog makes (TVC actuators, named programs Castor 30/Centaur/Ares/Antares), weak for market share. Confirms merchant TVC actuator tier on non-SpaceX programs.

evidence.excerpt: Moog designed and manufactured new hydraulic actuators for the thrust vector control system first stage main engines.
evidence.limitations: Moog press release (vendor). Establishes Moog as the TVC-actuator maker for ULA Vulcan first-stage engines (merchant tier), explicitly NOT SpaceX.

evidence.title: Wikipedia — SpaceX Super Heavy thrust vector control (hydraulic-to-electric)
evidence.summary: Super Heavy's inner 13 Raptor engines have gimbal actuators (outer 20 fixed); after Starship flight 1 the gimbaling system was switched from hydraulic to electric, removing the hydraulic power units — i.e. SpaceX's engine TVC actuation is in-house and now electric.
evidence.excerpt: The inner thirteen engines are equipped with gimbal actuators and reignite for the boostback and landing burns. The outer 20 engines, arranged in a ring, are fixed in place. ... After Starship's first flight test, this gimbaling system was switched from a hydraulic system to an electric one, enabling the removal of the hydraulic power units.
evidence.limitations: Wikipedia is a grey/pointer source per whitelist — used here only to evidence the captive (in-house, electric) nature of SpaceX engine TVC, a structural/qualitative fact, not a market number. Corroborated by Musk public statements; upgrade to primary in later round if needed.

This builds on previous contracts to supply SpaceX with 3D printers. SpaceX has used 3D printing in its Raptor engines.

evidence.summary: Eaton supplies high-performance propellant storage tanks for space propulsion (selected by MDA Space for the MDA AURORA satellite product line), providing secure fuel storage and transfer to the propulsion system — evidence of Eaton's space-propulsion fluid-hardware merchant role.
evidence.excerpt: Eaton's propellant storage tanks will provide secure fuel storage in addition to safe and efficient transfer of fuel to the satellite's propulsion system during orbit.
evidence.limitations: Trade-press; the fetched quote is a SATELLITE propulsion-tank selection, not a launch-vehicle valve/tank supply. Eaton's launch-vehicle hydraulic-pump heritage is real but its 2016 page was unreachable this round. Edge kept as reported_capable_supplier at low confidence.
